keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Pannonian march: the land is the Avar Khaganate to 805, then Bavarians/East Franks). 828-906: the Danube frontier and Upper Pannonia; Lower Pannonia under Pribina's and Kocel's principality is a vassal tint in the ledger (839-900). The page gives no area and no boundary; modern provinces are the reading. In 882-885 the Wilhelminer War was fought inside the march without a change of border.

ledger.note: 828: An Imperial Diet deposes Baldric of Friuli and sets apart the March of Pannonia as a frontier against Moravia within the Bavarian regnum. 'Louis the Pious granted Bavaria with Avaria to Louis the German' in 817; the Diet of 828 'set apart' the march. The page's infobox says only 'mid-9th century'.

region.text: Lower Pannonia 'between the Drava and Sava', Pribina's and Kocel's principality around Zalavár, 'northwest to the Rába and Ptuj, and southeast to the Baranya region and the Danube'

ledger.note: 839: Louis the German establishes the Slavic Duchy of Lower Pannonia under Pribina, with his residence at Zalavár on Lake Balaton. The Principality of Lower Pannonia page dates the Frankish count Radbod's deposition of Ratimir and the installation of Pribina to 838.

region.text: Lower Pannonia 'between the Drava and Sava', Pribina's and Kocel's principality around Zalavár, 'northwest to the Rába and Ptuj, and southeast to the Baranya region and the Danube'

ledger.note: c. 900: The Frankish domination of Lower Pannonia 'lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)'; Braslav, last dux of Lower Pannonia 884-896, ruled under Arnulf of Carinthia's overlordship, and Arnulf handed Pannonia to him in 895 or 896 against the Hungarians; 'no further Slavic rulers are recorded' after 907.

region.text: the Danube frontier 'from the Traungau and Carantania to Szombathely and the Rába, including the Vienna Basin': Upper Pannonia from the Enns and the Vienna Woods (a reading by modern provinces; the Enns line is the western edge)

ledger.note: 907: The Magyars destroy the Bavarian army at Pressburg and take the March of Pannonia. The battle was fought 4-6 July 907: Luitpold 'lost the March of Pannonia to them', 'almost all the soldiers, together with Luitpold' were massacred; the Enns became the boundary and 'all East Frankish lands beyond the Enns were lost' (March page).

ledger.note: 907: The March of Pannonia ends with Luitpold's death at Pressburg. The March page says that by the 890s the march 'seems to have disappeared' as a working unit, which is why the dossier is thin after 893.

wars.name: Wilhelminer War
wars.outcome: A rebellion of the Wilhelminer sons (Engelschalk II) against the margrave Aribo; Svatopluk of Moravia invaded Pannonia as Aribo's ally; Charles the Fat received Svatopluk as his vassal at Kaumberg (about 884); the Moravians and Arnulf agreed only in late 885.
wars.note: The page names no border change and no land beyond 'Pannonia'.

wars.outcome: Hungarian victory on 4-6 July 907: the East Frankish (mainly Bavarian) army was annihilated, Luitpold killed, the March of Pannonia lost and the Enns became the frontier.

certainty.note: A frontier march against the Avar lands and Moravia: the pages give rivers and towns (Enns, Rába, Szombathely, Drava, Sava), never a surveyed frontier.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from four pages (March of Pannonia, Principality of Lower Pannonia, Battle of Pressburg, Wilhelminer War). 828 (the Diet that set the march apart) is the start; the page's infobox says 'mid-9th century' and no end, so 907 (Pressburg) is the end though the page says the march 'seems to have disappeared' by the 890s. Overlaps: Cliopatria draws Great Moravia (814-910), the Avar Khaganate (to 805), Carantania (661-749), the Magyars (840-910) and the Principality of Hungary (900-999) near this land, and the East Franks 850-910 shape probably covers it; the compile must subtract this march from the East Franks shape. The Principality of Lower Pannonia (Pribina, Kocel, Braslav, c. 838-c. 900, capital Mosapurc/Zalavár) has its own dossier in this batch (principality-of-lower-pannonia), the vassal counterpart here. Not on the pages (not drawn): the Avar March 796-828 (Gerold of Bavaria, Pippin of Italy's Ring: not in the page text), Kocel and Methodius dates, 856 Carloman's fortifications as border moves, 871 Carloman's gift of Upper Pannonia to Aribo (internal), 876 Arnulf's Lower Pannonia (a change of overlord inside the vassal tint), the Wilhelminer sons' homage to Arnulf. The Wilhelminer War page says Svatopluk intervened as Aribo's ally and later became Charles the Fat's vassal, so no contest with great-moravia is booked. Gazetteer: no region named Pannonia; modern provinces are used (Niederösterreich, Wien, Burgenland, Vas (Szombathely), Gyor-Moson-Sopron, Zala; reviewer eu-07-x replaced the one-cell urban counties Szombathely and Nagykanizsa with the Vas and Zala counties the notes meant, Somogy, Baranya, Ptuj). Names needed: regions Pannonia, Upper Pannonia, Lower Pannonia; places Zalavár, Tulln. Capitals are empty: the pages name no seat of the margraves (Tulln is first documented in 859; Herzogenburg and Wilhelmsburg were fortified under Carloman after 856). Wikidata left null.
